'''Peter van Nieuwenhuizen''' ({{IPA|nl|ˈpeːtər vɑ ˈniu.ə(n)ˌɦœyzə(n)|lang}}; born 26 October 1938) is a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] [[physicist|theoretical physicist]]. He is a distinguished Professor at [[Stony Brook University]] in the [[United States]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stony Brook Physics & Astronomy Faculty - Peter van Nieuwenhuizen |url=http://insti.physics.sunysb.edu/physics/forms/profilesearch.cgi?lastname=van%20nieuwenhuizen |access-date=16 November 2023 |website=insti.physics.sunysb.edu}}</ref> Van Nieuwenhuizen is widely known for his contributions to [[string theory]], [[supersymmetry]], [[supergravity]] and [[Quantum field theory|field theory]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Peter van Nieuwenhuizen in nLab |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Peter+van+Nieuwenhuizen |access-date=16 November 2023 |website=ncatlab.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/985020 |access-date=16 November 2023 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=P. van Nieuwenhuizen |url=https://research.com/u/p-van-nieuwenhuizen |access-date=15 November 2023 |website=research.com}}</ref>

He is best known for his discovery of [[supergravity]] with [[Sergio Ferrara]] and [[Daniel Z. Freedman]], for which he along with his collaborators won the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Peter van Nieuwenhuizen |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L3851 |access-date=16 November 2023 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Peter van Nieuwenhuizen studied physics and mathematics at the University of Utrecht, where he obtained in 1971 his Ph.D. under the supervision of later Nobel laureate [[Martinus Veltman]].<ref name="Niels Bohr Library & Archives">{{cite web | title=Van Nieuwenhuizen, Peter | website=Niels Bohr Library & Archives | url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11610028.html | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref> 

After his studies in Utrecht, Van Nieuwenhuizen went to [[CERN]] (Geneva), the University of Paris in Orsay, and [[Brandeis University]] (Waltham). In 1975 he joined the Institute for Theoretical Physics, now named [[C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics]], of the [[Stony Brook University]], where he succeeded Nobel laureate [[C. N. Yang]] as its director from 1999 until 2002.

He is married to Belgian physicist Marie de Crombrugghe.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dunaief |first=Daniel |date=23 August 2019 |title=SBU’s van Nieuwenhuizen shares $3M for 43-year-old theory {{!}} TBR News Media |url=https://tbrnewsmedia.com/sbus-van-nieuwenhuizen-shares-3m-for-43-year-old-theory/ |access-date=23 December 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Van Hal |first=George |date=22 November 2019 |title=De Nederlandse natuurkundige die op zijn 81ste de ‘Oscar van de wetenschap won’ |url=https://www.volkskrant.nl/wetenschap/de-nederlandse-natuurkundige-die-op-zijn-81ste-de-oscar-van-de-wetenschap-won~b0ca9024 |access-date=23 December 2025 |website=[[De Volkskrant]]}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
For constructing [[supergravity]], the first [[supersymmetric]] extension of Einstein's theory of [[general relativity]], and for their central role in its subsequent development
Peter van Nieuwenhuizen, [[Sergio Ferrara]] and [[Daniel Z. Freedman]] received in 1993 the [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac medal]] from the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in Trieste (Italy), in 2006 the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] of the [[American Physical Society]] and in 2016 the [[Ettore Majorana Medal]] from EMFCSC, Erice. In 2019, the three were awarded a special [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] of $3 million for the discovery.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Supergravity scientists share $3M US Breakthrough Prize |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/supergravity-breakthrough-prize-1.5237900 |work=CBC News}}</ref><ref name="Ball 2019">{{cite web | last=Ball | first=Philip | title=Supergravity Snags Super Award: $3-Million Special Breakthrough Prize | website=Scientific American | date=6 August 2019 | url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/supergravity-snags-super-award-3-million-special-breakthrough-prize/ | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>

He is a fellow of the American Physical Society, and a corresponding member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 1994,<ref name="KNAW">{{cite web | title=Nieuwenhuizen, Prof. dr. P. van (Peter) | website=KNAW | url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/correspondenten/4592 | language=nl | access-date=14 December 2021 | archive-date=20 May 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190520071422/https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/correspondenten/4592 | url-status=dead }}</ref> and of the Austrian Academy of Sciences. He was made a Knight in the Order of the Dutch Lion in 2004, and Honorary professor of the [[Technical University of Vienna]] (Austria) in 2005.
